$comment: This file IS the architecture. `pnpm guard:boundaries` fails CI when a package.json
declares a workspace dependency not listed in its `allow` array.
A rule you cannot break by accident is worth more than a rule in a README.
Layers: lower tiers may never depend on higher tiers. See docs/PACKAGE_MAP.md.

money.why: Fixed-point USDC arithmetic. Zero dependencies, zero I/O, zero floating point. Every other package's correctness rests on this one, so it must be trivially auditable.

protocol.why: HCS message schemas, version tags, and the canonical serializer used for the ceiling input hash. Schema-only: if this package could do I/O, the wire format could drift from what we publish.

params.why: Versioned credit parameters (tier multiples, APRs, ramp steps, caps, AGE_FULL_DAYS). Published as a pinned MODEL_VERSION because verify-ceiling must recompute with byte-identical inputs.

ledger.why: Pure double-entry accounting: holds, debits, credits, netting, interest accrual, invariant assertions. No database. The money math is tested as functions, not as a service.

scoring.why: effective revenue -> tier -> ceiling, as pure functions over already-fetched inputs. Purity is the product requirement, not a preference: a stranger running verify-ceiling has only HCS + Mirror Node, so scoring must not reach for our Postgres.

graph.why: Funding ancestry, control clusters, counterparty weights as pure functions over edge lists. Same purity reason as scoring; the caller supplies the edges.

hedera.why: The only package allowed to import the Hedera SDK. Wraps client construction, HTS transfers, HCS submit/read, and the HIP-423 schedule builder.

mirror.why: Mirror Node REST client: typed, paginated, timestamp-ranged. Deliberately separate from `hedera` so the fast path can depend on consensus-side code without inheriting the ability to make a history call.

cache.why: Redis: hold reservations, ceiling snapshot, circuit breaker. Fails closed by contract - a cache miss is a refusal, never an allow.

db.why: Drizzle schema + migrations for the counterparty graph and read models. HCS is the source of truth; this is a rebuildable projection.

x402.why: Adapter over the @x402 v2 packages for all three roles we play: client (spend leg), resource server (earn leg), self-hosted facilitator (earn leg settlement). Isolated because @x402 is a fast-moving dependency.

observability.why: Logger, trace context, metrics. Depends on nothing so every layer may depend on it.

fastpath.why: THE HOT PATH. Target under 50ms, cache and memory only. The README calls the no-Mirror-Node rule an architectural ban; this deny list is that ban made mechanical. It also cannot reach Postgres, the SDK, or the scoring code - it reads a precomputed snapshot and decides.

sdk.why: Public TypeScript client an agent installs. Must stay thin and browser-safe: no Hedera SDK, no Redis, no database driver. It speaks HTTP to the gateway.

agentkit-plugin.why: Hedera Agent Kit v4 Plugin (spend/quote/balance/ceiling tools) plus an AbstractPolicy subclass that blocks at the tool boundary. Built on the SDK, not on internals, so it stays publishable.

mcp.why: MCP server exposing the same verbs to any MCP-capable runtime. Same rule as the plugin: SDK only.

testkit.why: Fixtures, a fake unmodified x402 seller, a fake payer, deterministic clocks, and testcontainers helpers. Dev-only; never a runtime dependency of an app.

gateway.why: Deployable. Fastify: spend leg (x402 client), earn leg (x402 resource server), self-hosted facilitator, HCS receipt writer, hold manager.

engine.why: Deployable worker. The slow path: Mirror indexer -> graph -> scoring -> publish ceiling to HCS -> write cache snapshot. May shrink a ceiling mid-window; may never grow one.

settlement.why: Deployable worker. Window tick, HIP-423 schedule construction, and the reconciler that diffs Mirror outbound transfers against the receipt topic.

cli.why: Deployable. Operator surface: register, inspect, dump receipts, force a settlement in demo mode.

dashboard.why: Deployable Next.js app. Reads through the SDK only. A browser bundle must never be able to import a signing key path or a database driver.

verify.why: THE TRUST ARTIFACT. verify-tab and verify-ceiling must be runnable by a stranger who has our repo and nothing else - no Postgres, no Redis, no gateway. This deny list is what makes that claim true instead of aspirational.

probes.why: Phase 0. Writes docs/probes.md. Runs before any other code exists, so it depends only on adapters.

bootstrap.why: One-time environment setup: create HCS topics, associate the USDC token, fund the hot float, register demo sellers.

honest-agent.why: Demo agent. The SDK-only rule is the demo's central claim: this agent holds no key and signs nothing, so it must not even be able to import the Hedera SDK.

loop-attacker.why: Demo adversary, operated by a second party. It DOES get the Hedera SDK, because standing up a seller it controls is the whole point of the attack.
